page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at the top, with the page number 114 at the top left. Section numbers (§920, §319, §324) in the left margin. No notes in the right margin, no catchword, no signature.

main_text.p: Davidem æstimatione habitus; ut, quidquid diceret, §920.de cœlo prolatum ducerctur: (unde & de factione ejus David tantopere consternatus est, ut nullo unquam periculo magis:) quoniam videbat, populum adhuc quadam erga Davidem religione teneri; & non posse adduci, ut crederet, Absolonem filium tanto patrem odio habere, ut extremum ejus exitium quæreret: imo & merito, ne, si reconcilientur, faba in ipsorum caput cudatur: primum impudentissimus Absoloni fuit auctor, torum paternum luce clara coram populo contaminandi: ut hoc facto declararet, pessime ipsum velle patri, nec ex composito rem geri. Post fœdatam patris cubile, eidem consulit, ut patrem imparatum citra omnem moram armis obruat, nec ullum ipsi tempus ad vires recolligendas permittat. Quod suum consilium ubi videbat sperni: Chusajo contrarium suadente, & probabiliores moras interponendas causas afferre viso: victus partim indignatione, partim vano metu supplicii sibi irrogandi, se David regnum recuperaret: laqueo seipsum domi suæ strangulavit: atque ita proditionis & mali consilii sui dignas dedit pœnas: horrendo relicto exemplo, quàm tragico casu pereant malorum consiliorum architecti, & quàm sæpe divinitus ea impediantur. 2.Reg.16.17.

§319.Sic & Haman, patefactis calumniis, quibus impetraverat edictum Regis Persici, de tota gente Judæorum delenda, in ea ipsa furca, quam Mardochæo erexerat, ipse suspensus est: atque ita in magistrum scelera redierunt sua. Esth.7.

p.i: Circumretit enim vis atque injuria quemque:
Atque unde exorta est, ad eum plerumque revertit:

main_text.p: Sic & Appius Claudius Decemvir, ubi Virginiæ castitatem, undiquaque pudicitiâ septam, muneribus & pollicitis expugnare non potuit: dum illam in servitutem, spe ipsius potiundæ, per M. page.notes: The left-margin section numbers are read as "§920", "§319" and "§324"; the "§" and the first digit are uncertain, so they carry no [?] in the text but should be checked. The word "ducerctur" is a probable misreading of "ducereetur" and is printed as it appears. The Lucretius line is marked as a reference only; the verse itself is not in the scan. The running head "CORONÆ III" is taken from the page head; the Æ ligature is uncertain.
